title: Model Context Protocol (MCP) integration in Freshdesk
snippet:
The Freshworks Model Context Protocol (MCP) server enables AI tools like Cursor and Claude to securely connect and interact with Freshdesk. The MCP server acts as middleware to expose specific capabilities, such as creating tickets, by using public APIs and supported authentication methods.

Note: Currently, Freshdesk allows you to authenticate requests involved in MCP integration by using an API key only.

```
This feature applies to the following products:
• Freshdesk Standalone 2021 (Latest version)
• Freshdesk Unified Omni 2026
```
Starting September 10, 2026, the Freshworks MCP integration is generally available. The rate limits and monthly action allowances for each plan are outlined below.
```
What counts as an MCP action?
An action is defined as a successful tool invocation via MCP. Examples of tool invocations. Examples:
• Fetch conversation related to the ticket with ID 1001 (1 action)
• Update the company name for the record with ID 11 to Apple (1 action)
```
| Supported plans | Rate limits (actions per minute) | Included MCP actions (per account, annually) |
|---|---|---|
| Growth | 25 | 1,200 |
| Pro | 50 | 6,000 |
| Enterprise | 100 | 12,000 |
```
Important:
• Pricing: To view current pricing and purchase add-on action packs, see Pricing.
• EAP transition:
• If you were on the Early Access Program (EAP), standard pricing and limits take effect on October 5, 2026.
• During the EAP, if you used the MCP integration on any plan other than Freshdesk Standalone 2021 (the latest version) or Freshdesk Unified Omni 2026 variant, the integration will stop working after September 10, 2026.
```

snippet:

An MCP server implementation that integrates with Freshdesk, enabling AI models to interact with Freshdesk modules and perform various support operations.
## Features
- **Freshdesk Integration**: Seamless interaction with Freshdesk API endpoints
- **AI Model Support**: Enables AI models to perform support operations through Freshdesk
- **Automated Ticket Management**: Handle ticket creation, updates, and responses
## Components
### Tools
The server offers several tools for Freshdesk operations:
- `create_ticket`: Create new support tickets
- **Inputs**:
- `subject` (string, required): Ticket subject
- `description` (string, required): Ticket description
- `source` (number, required): Ticket source code
- `priority` (number, required): Ticket priority level
- `status` (number, required): Ticket status code
- `email` (string, optional): Email of the requester
- `requester_id` (number, optional): ID of the requester
- `custom_fields` (object, optional): Custom fields to set on the ticket
- `additional_fields` (object, optional): Additional top-level fields
- `update_ticket`: Update existing tickets
- **Inputs**:
- `ticket_id` (number, required): ID of the ticket to update
- `ticket_fields` (object, required): Fields to update
- `delete_ticket`: Delete a ticket
- **Inputs**:
- `ticket_id` (number, required): ID of the ticket to delete
- `search_tickets`: Search for tickets based on criteria
- **Inputs**:
- `query` (string, required): Search query string
- `get_ticket_fields`: Get all ticket fields
- **Inputs**:
- None
- `get_tickets`: Get all tickets
- **Inputs**:
- `page` (number, optional): Page number to fetch
- `per_page` (number, optional): Number of tickets per page
- `get_ticket`: Get a single ticket
- **Inputs**:
- `ticket_id` (number, required): ID of the ticket to get
- `get_ticket_conversation`: Get conversation for a ticket
- **Inputs**:
- `ticket_id` (number, required): ID of the ticket
- `create_ticket_reply`: Reply to a ticket

### Installing via Smithery
To install freshdesk_mcp for Claude Desktop automatically via [Smithery](https://smithery.ai/server/@effytech/freshdesk_mcp):
```
npx -y @smithery/cli install @effytech/freshdesk_mcp --client claude
```

title: MCP Integration: Frequently asked questions (FAQ)
snippet:
The Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open standard that enables AI assistants, such as Claude and Microsoft Copilot, to connect directly to Freshdesk. Through MCP, these assistants can perform actions on your behalf, such as creating tickets, updating contacts, or retrieving conversation history, without leaving the AI client.
Which Freshdesk products support MCP?
MCP is supported only in Freshdesk 2021 and Freshdesk Unified Omni 2026. Following is the compatibility matrix:
| **Product / Plan Variant** | **GA Support (Post-Sep 10, 2026)** | **Notes** |
|---|---|---|
| Freshdesk Standalone 2021 (Latest version) | Supported | Full support for GA release. |
| Freshdesk Unified Omni 2026 | Supported | Full support for GA release. |
| Legacy Freshdesk Variants (Pre-2021) / Other SKUs | Not Supported | EAP access ends September 10, 2026. |
Which AI clients are supported?
You can use any AI client that supports the MCP standard. Connect your preferred MCP-compatible client to Freshdesk using the MCP server URL and the API key provided in your Freshdesk administrator settings.
### Setup and configuration
How do I find my MCP settings in Freshdesk?
Go to Admin Settings > Apps & Integrations > MCP. On the MCP Details page, you can copy your MCP server URL, generate an API key, and manage your connection.
Is MCP enabled by default?
Yes. MCP is enabled by default for your Freshdesk instance. Administrators can disable it at any time from the MCP Details page.
How does authentication work for MCP?
Freshdesk MCP uses API key authentication. Each user manually connects their AI client using their individual Freshdesk API key and the MCP server URL. You can find your API key in your Freshdesk profile settings.

To connect an AI client to Freshdesk via MCP, you must manually enter the MCP server URL and authenticate using your API key.

title: Freshworks Developer Platform Docs
snippet:
The Freshworks Developer MCP server provides a standardized interface for managing the app lifecycle and submissions. Currently, it is being used by the **fw-publish** skill to enable AI assistants to interact securely with the Developer Portal to automate discovery, status tracking, and package uploads.
## Overview of architecture
The Developer MCP server works in the following way:
1. The **MCP client** (such as Cursor, Claude, or GitHub Copilot) includes an AI agent powered by a large language model (LLM).
2. The AI agent communicates with the Developer MCP server using the **Model Context Protocol (MCP)**.
3. The MCP server then interacts with internal tools through APIs to provide Freshworks-specific assistance.

### Prerequisites
Before you begin, make sure you have the following:
- An active Freshworks Developer Account, if you don't already have one, [Sign Up](https://developers.freshworks.com/signup/) to create a new account
- **FDK** version 9.1.0 or later. We recommend using the latest version of the **FDK**
- A working understanding of the Model Context Protocol (MCP)
- Familiarity with MCP clients, such as Cursor, Visual Studio Code, or other MCP-compatible tools
### Create and set up the MCP JSON configuration
Follow the steps below to create and set up the MCP JSON configuration required for connecting to the server:
1. Go to the [Application Management Portal](https://developers.freshworks.com/login/) (**AMP**) and click the **Settings** icon in the top-right corner.
2. Under the **API key for Freddy AI Copilot VS Code plugin & Agentic Developer Toolkit** section, click **Generate API Key** or **View API Key**.
3. The API key is displayed.
4. Add the following details to the MCP configuration file of your preferred AI assistant:
- **Name**: fw-dev-mcp
- **URL**: https://mcp.freshworks.dev/mcp
- **Authorization header**: Your Developer API key obtained from the Application Management Portal.
#### Sample MCP JSON configuration code
```json
{
"mcpServers": {
"fw-dev-mcp": {
"url": "https://mcp.freshworks.dev/mcp",
"headers": {
"Authorization": "Bearer <your-api-key>"
}
}
}
}
```
Once the MCP server is set up, the tools listed in the [Available tools](https://developers.freshworks.com/docs/agentic-dev-tools/mcp-server/#list-of-available-tools) section are available for the AI assistant to use.
## Rate limits
Requests to the Developer MCP server are limited to **60 requests per minute**.
